update.title: Reduced XFCE forks while moving to 4.20
update.summary: Archived an unchanged clipboard-manager copy, rebased three focused panel patches onto XFCE 4.20, and retained the systemd-scope integration that still had no upstream equivalent.

blocks.body:
## Decide separately for each fork

I audited three XFCE components before moving the desktop to the 4.20 line. The clipboard-manager copy matched upstream, so I archived it. The panel still needed three focused patches—for a fixed-size child, configurable show-desktop width, and Wayland pointer safety—so I rebased those changes onto the newer upstream branch. The libxfce4ui fork stayed in place because its systemd-scope launching still had no upstream equivalent.

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  Audit[Audit each component] --> Difference{Local behavior still needed?}
  Difference -->|No| Archive[Archive unchanged copy]
  Difference -->|Focused patch set| Rebase[Rebase panel onto XFCE 4.20]
  Difference -->|No upstream equivalent| Retain[Keep systemd integration fork]
  Archive --> Verify[Verify migrated desktop session]
  Rebase --> Verify
  Retain --> Verify
blocks.description: The migration disposition followed the actual delta of each component rather than one fleet-wide rule.

blocks.body:
## Preserve the panel behavior on the new base

The rebase kept the thin-strip layout, the 10-pixel show-desktop width, and the Wayland crash fixes while taking the upstream changes around them. I backed up the live XFCE configuration, built the custom panel, loaded all 15 plugins, verified the button-width property, and observed the migrated session without errors.

The result is a smaller, explicit maintenance surface: no fork where there is no difference, three isolated panel patches where the layout still depends on them, and one retained library fork for systemd-scoped application launches.
